d: We are looking for an Accountant to join our team, with experience in financial accounting within the real estate development industry. Candidates with experience in the government sector will also be considered an advantage.
q: Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
Experience in real estate development is required.
Experience in the government sector is preferred but not mandatory.
Good knowledge of accounting principles and financial reporting.
Proficiency in accounting software and MS Excel.
r: Manage day-to-day accounting operations and financial transactions.
Prepare and maintain financial records, reports, and reconciliations.
Handle accounts payable, accounts receivable, and general ledger entries.
Assist with monthly, quarterly, and annual financial closings.
Ensure accuracy of financial documentation and compliance with applicable accounting standards.
Support budgeting, financial reporting, and audit processes.
Coordinate with internal departments to ensure smooth financial operations

d: The Senior Quantity Surveyor, Joinery provides proactive commercial and cost management across assigned joinery manufacturing projects, from project handover through execution and final account.

The role establishes effective cost controls, forecasts project commercial performance, identifies budget gaps, margin exposure and contractual risks at an early stage, and supports appropriate mitigation and commercial recovery actions.

Working closely with Project Management, Manufacturing, Procurement, Estimation and Finance, the Senior QS provides commercial insight and cost visibility to support timely decision-making and protect project margins, while maintaining clear accountability boundaries across the respective functions.
q: Bachelor’s degree in Quantity Surveying, Commercial Management, Civil Engineering or a related discipline.
Approximately 7 to 10 years of relevant quantity surveying or commercial experience, preferably within joinery, interior fit-out, furniture manufacturing or hospitality interiors.

Demonstrable experience in project budgeting, Cost-to-Complete forecasting, variation and change management, procurement commercial control, client valuations, contract administration and final accounts.
Strong ability to analyse cost and margin movement, identify commercial risk early and translate commercial information into practical management recommendations.
Good understanding of GCC commercial practices, supplier markets and contractual environments.
Strong analytical, negotiation, communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and commercial reporting tools; ERP or project cost-control system experience would be an advantage.
Professional accreditation such as MRICS, AIQS or equivalent would be an advantage.
Performance Should Be Assessed Through a Balanced Combination Of
Accuracy and timeliness of project cost forecasts;
Early identification and escalation of budget and margin exposure;
Effective identification, substantiation and recovery of variations;
Alignment between approved budgets, commitments, actual costs and forecast outcomes;
Quality and timeliness of commercial reporting and payment applications;
Timely commercial close-out and final account settlement;
Quality of cost and commercial feedback provided to Estimation and other functions; and
Implementation of agreed commercial mitigation and improvement actions.

Shared-outcome principle: Project profitability remains a shared business outcome influenced by Estimation, Project Management, Procurement, Manufacturing, Finance and other project stakeholders and should not be considered the sole responsibility of the Senior QS.
r: Participate in the commercial handover of awarded projects, reviewing tender assumptions, scope, budgets, procurement and manufacturing allowances, contractual obligations and identified risks.
Establish and maintain the project commercial baseline, providing clear visibility of approved budgets, commitments, actual costs, forecast costs, variations and projected margin.
Maintain accurate Cost-to-Complete and Estimate-at-Completion forecasts and identify emerging budget gaps, margin erosion and commercial exposure at an early stage.
Analyse the causes of cost movement and work with relevant stakeholders to recommend mitigation, recovery or corrective actions.
Escalate material commercial risks sufficiently early to allow appropriate management intervention.
Proactively identify changes to the contracted or approved scope and assess their commercial and contractual implications.
Ensure variation entitlement and cost exposure are identified, documented and communicated before significant cost is incurred, wherever practicable.
Prepare, substantiate and track variations, claims and commercial submissions through to resolution.
Monitor contractual obligations, notice requirements, payment provisions and other conditions affecting the company’s commercial position.
Maintain clear and auditable commercial records to support contractual entitlement and final account settlement.
Monitor procurement and subcontract commitments against approved project budgets and allowances.
Provide commercial review of supplier and subcontractor quotations, identifying scope gaps, exclusions, qualifications and material budget variances.
Review payment applications, variation claims and final accounts against agreed terms, verified progress and approved scope.
Monitor the commercial impact of material usage, labour, subcontract activities, rework, waste and production changes.
Work with Procurement, Manufacturing and Project Management to identify cost exposure and evaluate commercially viable mitigation opportunities without assuming their functional responsibilities.
Prepare client payment applications and supporting commercial documentation in accordance with contractual requirements and verified project progress.
Maintain billing, collection and project cash-flow forecasts in coordination with Project Management and Finance.
Produce concise commercial reports covering cost and margin movement, risks, opportunities, mitigation actions and projected project outcome.
Provide early warning of adverse commercial trends and clearly communicate the financial impact, recommended action and required management decision.
Provide structured commercial and cost feedback to Tendering and Estimation based on actual project performance.
Share relevant intelligence on material and subcontract costs, procurement trends, manufacturing cost drivers, budget variances, commercial risks and lessons learned.
Participate in post-project reviews and selected bid reviews where actual project experience can improve future pricing and commercial strategy.
Provide commercial intelligence and feedback without replacing Estimation’s responsibility for quantity take-off, rate build-up, tender pricing and submission preparation.
Develop and maintain the commercial close-out and final account strategy for assigned projects.
Progressively resolve variations, claims, retentions, supplier and subcontractor accounts and other outstanding commercial matters.
Reconcile final project performance against tender assumptions, approved budgets and forecast outcomes.
Capture and communicate commercial lessons learned to Project Management, Estimation, Procurement, Manufacturing and Management.
Identify recurring cost leakage, commercial-control gaps and opportunities to improve project handover, forecasting, variation management and cost visibility.
